title: Why is the sky blue?
style_lock: clean flat vector illustration, geometric shapes, soft gradients allowed only in the background, limited modern palette of sky blue, sunset orange and warm white, crisp edges, friendly rounded shapes

beats.line: Ever wondered why the sky is blue and not green or pink?
beats.scene: a wide open sky over gentle green hills, with a child's kite flying high
beats.action: the kite is the main subject, centred
beats.caption: Why is the sky blue?

beats.line: Sunlight looks white, but it is really every colour mixed together.
beats.scene: a bright sun shining a white beam into a glass prism on a table, the beam spreading into a rainbow fan
beats.caption: Sunlight = every colour mixed

beats.line: When it hits the air, tiny bits of air bounce the colours around.
beats.scene: a close-up of the air drawn as tiny round particles with coloured light rays bouncing off them in all directions
beats.action: a cluster of particles in the centre
beats.caption: Air bounces light around

beats.line: Blue light is bounced the most, so blue reaches your eyes from every direction.
beats.scene: a person standing in a field looking up, many blue light rays arriving from every part of the sky
beats.action: the person is seen from behind, centred
beats.caption: Blue bounces the most

beats.line: At sunset, light travels through much more air, so the reds and oranges win.
beats.scene: a glowing orange and pink sunset over the sea, the sun low on the horizon
beats.action: the sun is centred on the horizon
beats.caption: Sunset: reds and oranges win

beats.line: Now you know. Look up, and tell someone why!
beats.scene: two friends lying on the grass pointing up at a clear blue sky with a few white clouds
beats.caption: Look up and tell someone why!
